prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a small enclosed room with a recessed wall shelf on the left (~1.5–2.5 m away in frame 1), a stone floor below, and two bare-chested men standing side by side (~0.2–0.4 m apart) in front of the camera wearer with their heads cropped out of the top of the frame. Across the five frames, the camera wearer approaches and tilts downward from ~1.5–2.0 m away in frame 1 to within ~0.3–0.6 m (well within arm's reach) by frames 3–5, while the two men lean forward and lower their arms toward a lit floor lamp below on the left and toward the wearer's lower body, and in frame 5 the wearer's right arm reaches forward from the bottom right to touch the left man's waist (~0.3 m away). Because the men's heads are out of view above the frame, gaze direction is not visible, though their torso surfaces angle toward the camera wearer and slightly left. Compared to the RGB strip, where harsh shadows and dark clothing obscure spatial boundaries, the depth gradients clearly separate the foreground raised palm and overlapping arms in frame 4 from the torsos behind them and capture the continuous distance gradient along the floor and shelf. However, the depth map becomes unreliable when the men are very close in frames 3–5, where the background floor drops into pure black and relative depth saturates to uniform white on the closest shoulders and chests.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the two standing men in front of the camera wearer in frames 1 and 2—putting the left man (~1.5–2.0 m shrinking to ~1.0–1.5 m) in pink and the slightly closer right man (~1.2–1.8 m shrinking to ~0.8–1.2 m, ~0.3 m to the right) in brown—as both face generally toward the camera wearer with heads cropped above the top edge. As the distance closes to within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) across frames 3 to 5, the two men bend down and their arms overlap in the foreground while the camera wearer's own right forearm enters from the bottom right in frame 5 to contact the left man's garment. While this map cleanly delineates the boundary between the two adjacent bodies in frames 1–2 and isolates the wearer's reaching arm as a distinct pink mask against the dark wrap in frame 5—which blends into dark shadows in RGB—it fails to segment the wall shelf, floor, or small lit lamp on the floor to the left. The map is heavily unreliable across the sequence: it mislabels the right man's shoulder and doorway edge in frame 1 as a 'fork', completely misses both men in frame 3 except for a tiny 'person' fragment at the bottom edge (a foot/garment edge), and merges both overlapping men and their intertwined arms into a single contiguous 'person' mask in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly blank across the five-frame approach toward the two standing men (~1.5–2.0 m away in frame 1 down to ~0.3–0.6 m in frame 5), capturing only isolated skeletal fragments where bodies and hands enter the camera view. In frame 1, a yellow body skeleton marks the torso and upper thighs of the left man standing ~1.8 m away facing toward and slightly left of the camera wearer, while in frame 3 a magenta hand skeleton locates his lowered left hand ~0.6 m away near his waist, within arm's reach of both men and the camera wearer. In frame 4, two magenta hand skeletons clearly resolve the 3D finger articulation and orientation of the left man's raised left palm (~0.3 m in front of the lens, facing the wearer) and his right hand reaching across the right man's lower arm (~0.4 m to the right and slightly further back), and in frame 5 a single magenta skeleton tracks the camera wearer's own right hand touching the left man's hip (~0.3 m away). These hand skeletons make the exact finger splay, palm orientation, and contact points much easier to read than in the motion-blurred, shadowed RGB frames. However, the pose estimator is highly unreliable wherever heads and limbs are cropped out of the frame or self-occluded, completely failing to detect the right-hand man in any frame, missing all bodies in frames 2–5, and collapsing the yellow head keypoints onto the left man's neck/chest in frame 1 because his head is out of view above the frame.
